aggressive_definition: Aggressive incident prostate cancer; the abstract does not report the clinical criteria used to define aggressive disease.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: 1226 incident cases of prostate cancer, 355 of them aggressive, were identified during 7.9 years of follow-up.
study_design: Prospective cohort study of Adventist men without prevalent cancer.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: In a prospective study of 27,934 Adventist men without prevalent cancer, Cox proportional hazard regression analyses were used to address the objectives.
reason: The initially cancer-free prospective cohort accrued incident prostate cancers and analyzed both overall incidence and aggressive versus non-aggressive incidence.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Consumption of canned and cooked tomatoes more than four times a week was associated with a HR = 0.72 (95% CI 0.55, 0.94, P = 0.02) comparing to risk in those never consuming this food.
estimate_classifications.reason: This estimate is for overall incident prostate cancer, not specifically aggressive disease. The abstract separately reports competing-risk analyses of aggressive and non-aggressive cancers.

additional_estimates.comparison: Tomato associations between aggressive and non-aggressive prostate cancers
additional_estimates.effect_excerpt: Uncalibrated multivariable-adjusted competing risk analyses do not find differences in tomato associations between aggressive and non-aggressive prostate cancers although power for aggressive cancers is limited.
additional_estimates.count_excerpt: 1226 incident cases of prostate cancer, 355 of them aggressive, were identified during 7.9 years of follow-up.
additional_estimates.endpoint_definition: Aggressive incident prostate cancer; clinical criteria were not provided in the abstract.
